content.title: About
content.content: The reduced‑sugar cookie sandwich consists of two thin cookies filled with a smooth cream. The recipe uses less sugar, often replaced by sweeteners such as stevia or erythritol, making it a better choice for people monitoring blood‑sugar levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cookie sandwich appeared in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became a popular treat.
Lower sugar content helps the cookies retain their shape longer because less crystallization occurs.
Whole‑grain flour is frequently used instead of white flour to cut calories and boost nutrition.
The cream may contain dairy proteins or plant‑based alternatives, increasing the product’s protein content.
Individual packaging makes the sandwich a convenient option for school lunchboxes.

items.title: Reduced sugar
items.content: Lower sugar helps control the glycemic index and reduces the risk of rapid blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour adds dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Whole grains provide slower‑digesting carbohydrates that keep you fuller longer.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: If nuts or seeds are included, they contribute monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The cream can be fortified with B‑vitamins and calcium, supporting energy metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Allergen ingredients
items.content: The product may contain wheat, milk, nuts, or soy, which are common allergens.

items.title: Sugar‑substitute side effects
items.content: Some sweeteners (e.g., sugar alcohols) can cause gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in excess.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Even with reduced sugar, the sandwich still provides calories from fats and carbs, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: If wheat flour is used, the product is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie sandwich as a quick snack, add it to a lunchbox, or pair it with fruit and yogurt. It can be gently warmed in the microwave to soften the cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sandwich in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep it refrigerated to prevent the cream from drying out. Discard if you notice mold or an off‑odor.

content.title: About
content.content: Crackers NFS are dry baked wafers made from wheat flour, vegetable oil, and salt. They have a light crunchy texture and a mild, slightly salty flavor, making them a convenient snack and a versatile base for various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cracker recipes appeared in the 19th century as a way to extend the shelf life of bread.
Crackers are often used in military rations because of their light weight and long shelf life.
In many countries crackers are served with cheese, pâté, or caviar as an appetizer.
NFS stands for “No Flour Substitute,” indicating the product contains only wheat flour.
Crackers can be made from whole grain or white flour; NFS uses only wheat flour.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Crackers provide quickly digestible carbs that can rapidly replenish energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many snack breads, NFS crackers contain little fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies modest amounts of B1, B2, and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The simple formulation makes crackers easy on the stomach and ideal for a light snack.

items.title: Portable
items.content: Their sturdy structure prevents crumbling, so they are convenient for travel and outdoor activities.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Crackers made from wheat flour contain gluten and may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapidly absorbable carbs can cause a quick spike in blood sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Some NFS varieties are quite salty; individuals monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Certain batches may contain preservatives or flavor enhancers that can cause individual intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be eaten plain, spread with cream cheese, hummus, pâté, or used as a base for canapés. They are also added to soups and salads for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any crackers that show signs of mold or off‑odors.

nutritional-drink-or-shake-ready-to-drin.title: Nutritional drink or shake, ready-to-drink, sugar free (Glucerna)

content.title: About
content.content: Glucerna is a ready‑to‑drink nutritional shake that is sugar‑free, formulated especially for people with pre‑diabetes and diabetes. It contains slowly digestible carbohydrates, high‑quality protein, and added vitamins and minerals to help maintain stable blood glucose levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Glucerna is produced by Abbott, a leader in medical nutrition.
The formula includes a protein hydrolysate that is quickly absorbed.
The product contains no added sugar and has a low glycemic index.
Each serving provides 10 g of protein, making it a convenient protein source.
Glucerna is available in several flavors, including vanilla and chocolate.

items.title: Supports blood glucose control
items.content: The blend of slowly digestible carbs and protein helps prevent rapid spikes in blood sugar.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: 10 g of high‑quality protein per serving supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The shake supplies B‑vitamins, vitamin D, calcium, and iron, essential for overall health.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: Ready‑to‑drink format provides quick nutrition without preparation.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Absence of added sugar makes it suitable for those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Glucerna contains dairy protein; individuals with milk allergy should avoid it.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: To replace sugar, the drink may contain sucralose or aspartame, which are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Not a complete meal replacement
items.content: While nutritious, the shake should not replace a varied diet.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume one packet (250 ml) immediately after mixing, or within 30 minutes after a meal. The shake can be used as a snack between meals or as a supplement to breakfast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the packets in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 48 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Onions (Allium cepa) are bulb vegetables made of concentric layers, native to Central Asia and cultivated for thousands of years. They come in yellow, white, red, and sweet varieties and have a pungent, sharp flavor when raw that turns sweet and mellow when cooked. Onions are a foundation of cooking in nearly every cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions are related to garlic, leeks, shallots, and chives.
Cutting an onion releases a sulfur compound that irritates the eyes and causes tearing.
Red onions get their color from anthocyanins.
Onions are among the most widely used vegetables in the world.
Chilling an onion or using a sharp knife can reduce tearing.

items.title: Contains quercetin
items.content: Onions are a source of quercetin, a flavonoid with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides vitamin C and vitamin B6
items.content: These nutrients support the immune system and metabolism.

items.title: Contains prebiotic fibers
items.content: Onions contain inulin and fructooligosaccharides, which feed beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Contains sulfur compounds
items.content: These plant compounds are being studied for their biological activity.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Onions add a lot of flavor with few calories.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Onions contain fructans, which may cause gas, bloating, or heartburn in sensitive individuals, including people who follow low-FODMAP diets.

items.title: Allergic reactions and irritation
items.content: Some people may be allergic to onions or experience irritation from handling them.

items.title: Breath odor
items.content: Raw onion can cause lingering breath odor.

items.title: Toxic to pets
items.content: Onions are toxic to dogs and cats, so keep them out of reach of pets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onions can be eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, or sautéed, caramelized, roasted, grilled, pickled, or added to soups, stews, sauces, and stir-fries. Soaking sliced raw onion in cold water can mellow its sharpness. Caramelizing slowly brings out natural sweetness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole onions in a cool, dry, dark, well-ventilated place, away from potatoes, where they keep for weeks to months. Wrap cut onions tightly and refrigerate them for about a week. Discard onions that are soft, moldy, or have a bad smell.
